Official development assistance, ODA, has also declined significantly from $38 billion in 2020 to $32 billion in 2023. with projections indicating continued downward trends. So at IBP, We firmly believe that coalitions in country at all different levels with all different actors, including government champions, are key. And the same is true across governments. And maybe a glimmer of hope, what we have seen in our work, and with this I will end, is that when we work, especially in closed civic space with more and more authoritarian governments, we don't give up. It's hard not to give up. So you find ways and sometimes working with subnational governments is the way to innovate, to showcase, and then to scale up. So finding new windows of opportunity is becoming challenging, but it's also, I think, part of all of our jobs to making real change in development.

Yes, thank you. And thank you for your question, especially on investments in, for example, defense industry and investment in social policy. I think we see this as one of our big challenges for the next period in the European Union. And maybe if I look at the way in which we can communicate also with our constituents, with our citizens, it's very important to make sure that when we talk about physical security, we also talk about social security. And these two elements should not be a trade-off. But at the same time, we see that if you discuss about policies for individuals, there's a lot more debate in society, should individuals have tax breaks, supports if they are in need, if they live in vulnerable situations, than the debate about this huge amount of money, which is a little bit out of your understanding and out of your scope, that would go to, in this case, to, for example, the defense industry. So we really have to make sure when we talk about these elements, that all of them are important and all of them cost a lot of money. And it should not be, the one should not be crowding out the other, in my personal opinion, because I think if we build onto physical security on the European continent, but at the same time, we do not work on social security, we do not work, and with social security, I mean all the elements of social policies, so this could be nutrition or education or housing, all the elements that people need to just have a good life and to be able to see some hope and some perspective for their future individually, not necessarily as a country, but individually. We should work on those policies as well and work on those policies, of course, that we discussed here that relates to international solidarity, international collaboration. And if we forget the last bits, which is the soft power, So this international collaboration and the social policies nationally, and only look at the hard power, I think we lose why we have a government that serves the people. So this, I think, is really the big challenge that we have for the near future. Thank you.
